messages:
maria: Morning — async checkin. What I did: adjusted alert thresholds for model-serving latency SLOs, ran a staging canary against the new eviction jitter, and fixed a broken runbook link. Blockers: still seeing transient 503 spikes on the dedicated pool when bursts exceed ~200 req/s; need detailed traces to confirm KV cache thrash. Today: pair with @alex on tracing, and prepare a rollback plan. /cc @jordan :wave;

alex: saw the 503s during the 02:10 UTC burst. I captured traces and a few flamegraphs — top-level suspect is eviction hotloops when prefix reuse spikes. Uploading artifacts shortly. Plan: add a small randomized jitter to eviction window and limit per-shard eviction ops. Running a focused load test at 11:30 PT.

jordan: thanks. I updated the runbook to include a temporary traffic-route workaround (route to fallback-1) and a short checklist for reproducing the spike locally. Left comments for the playbook entry about who to page.

nate: quick question — do we want to suppress noisy alerts like noisy:latency_p99 during the canary window? I can create a short suppression if so.

lucy: don't silence globally. Use a scoped suppression for the canary tag only. Nate, can you create the suppression with scope=canary and add an annotation referencing this thread? Also add an entry to the incident log when you do it.

nate: yep — creating now. Command I'm running: ```hcctl suppress create --alert noisy:latency_p99 --duration 10m --scope=canary --annot "canary jitter test / maria"```

deploy-bot: Deploy started by @alex at 2024-09-15T11:33Z: canary/batch-evict-jitter -> staging (pods: 6 -> 6)

oncall-bot: Pager muted for canary-tagged alerts until 1745550723 (10m)

maria: thanks everyone. If the 11:30 load test goes green, target a small prod canary at 13:00 PT. @lucy can you schedule a 20m post-rollout audit (error budget + tail logs)?

lucy: yep — I'll tail the logs and check error budget after 20m. If errors exceed 0.2% we'll rollback immediately. I'll post the checklist I use.

alex: uploaded flamegraphs & traces to thread: https://redwood.slack-files/fg-1745550123.png — the hot path is in `evict_shard_loop()` and shows correlated GC pauses on the host.

jordan: FYI I removed a couple of stale links from the runbook and added a short troubleshooting checklist specifically for 503 bursts (includes `tcpdump` snippet and `hcctl` queries).

nate: suppression created and annotated in the incident log. :thumbsup:

maria: blockers cleared for now? Alex — if you want extra eyes on the runbook tests or the rollback play, ping me and I can join the pairing session. Otherwise I'll mark this check-in as done later today.

alex: all set for now. Will ping if we see >1% errors during canary. Thanks all.
